question.knowledge_point: The Domain of a Sphere or Ellipsoid
question.problem: Given the sphere $(x-2)^{2}+(y+2)^{2}+{z}^{2}=5,$ what is the domain of $z=z(x,y)?$
question.worked_solution:
From the equation of the sphere, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2}+(y+2)^{2}+{z}^{2} & =5 \\ {z}^{2} & =5-((x-2)^{2}+(y+2)^{2}) \\ z & =\pm \sqrt{5-((x-2)^{2}+(y+2)^{2})}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}5-((x-2)^{2}+(y+2)^{2})\ge 0 \\ (x-2)^{2}+(y+2)^{2}\le 5\end{aligned}
$$

This inequality describes the interior and boundary of the circle 

$$
(x-2)^{2}+(y+2)^{2}=5
$$

which is a circle of radius $\sqrt{5}$ centered at $(2,-2)$ in the $xy$-plane.
